My role
Product Manager
For
Car dealerships in Canada

The dealership that remembers

Because a part nobody picks up helps nobody.

🧩The problem

A customer orders a car part. The dealership gets it and keeps it on the shelf. Then the customer simply forgets to come and pick it up. On top of that, dealerships want to offer a more complete follow-up of each car's warranty.

🛠️What I am building

A system for car dealerships that manages service appointments and auto parts sales through an AI agent. It reminds customers about their orders and talks to them, so nobody on the team has to chase customers one by one. The goal: fewer parts that are ordered and never picked up, and a more complete warranty follow-up.

📍Where it is today

A car dealership in Canada already uses it, and 5 more are waiting to start.

Macarena Vergara, osteopath and physio in Punta del Este
Her practice
Instagram (5,000+ followers)

Maketa Wellness

Rehab routines patients actually want to do.

🧩The problem

Macarena's patients used to get their routines as a PDF, and for a premium practice that never felt right. The training apps out there did not fit either: they feel like a gym, and rehab is a different mood, one where you should feel looked after.

🛠️What I built

So I built a simple app. The physio creates a routine for each patient and sends it by link, with no download and no account. For the patient it feels like being taken care of, not like training.

📈What happened

  • Macarena uses it with her real patients today.
  • According to her, patients follow their routines more than they did with the PDF.
“Now my patients feel like doing the exercises, and they improve faster.”
Macarena Vergara, osteopath and physio (translated from Spanish)

🚀What's next

Maketa Wellness is a growing project. Right now I am building two new pieces: a scheduling system, and a way to follow each patient's rehab, so we can measure what today is still an impression.

Ola, dónde estás?

Waves, no PhD in weather required.

🧩The problem

To go surfing today, you drive around hoping to find a wave or you try to decode complicated forecasts. Surfers just want to be in the water, not become meteorologists.

🛠️What I built

I built an app where you pick the kind of wave you love and it tells you where the closest one is. No math, no charts, just the answer.

Five types: Longboard (tablonera, gentle), Fun (divertida, calm with a bit more challenge), Intense (intensa, powerful), Radical (radical, extreme) and Any wave (la que sea).

📍Where it is today

It is live, and 10 surfers are testing it. They love the idea, and now we are checking the forecast against what we see in the water, which is the real test.

Acapedia

Because doctors have better things to do.

🧩The problem

Picture a US doctor. To keep their license they need CME credits, and getting them felt like a small, constant frustration: the sources lived in one place, the tests in another, and every extra click took time they simply didn't have. It was a side quest nobody had asked for.

“Nobody wants to spend time doing this. If you are a doctor, you don't have time to lose.”
A doctor I interviewed

🛠️What we built

So we brought everything together in one app: trusted sources, the test and the credits, all in the same place. The only hard part left was the test itself, and that is exactly how it should be.

📈What happened

  • In one year, 800 different doctors took the test and earned their credits, without leaving the app.
  • We spent $0 on ads. Doctors simply told other doctors, and later it even reached US universities.

Fábrica de Momentos by UNICEF

A new way to reach new people.

🧩The problem

UNICEF had one product, donations, and it wasn't reaching anyone new. The challenge was how to meet people who had never really been close to UNICEF.

💡The insight

We ran 100 surveys, then listened in 30 interviews with millennials. They were the audience UNICEF reached least, and the one that trusted it least. So instead of asking them for money, we wanted to give them something they would be glad to receive: a simpler, nicer way to feed their kids well.

🛠️What we built

Fábrica de Momentos (Moments Factory in English, my translation) is a 6-month subscription about cooking with kids. It comes with recipes, ways to organize them, a way to share your food moments and products delivered to your door, all paid month by month.

We also gave it a face: a brand and a character called Blupi. Today the theme is food, but next year it could be art.

📈What happened

  • In 3 months, 100 people who were new to UNICEF subscribed, and we spent nothing on paid advertising. We knew they were new because we checked UNICEF's own databases.
  • After that, UNICEF started paying for promotion.
  • Later, it was taken as a reference case for other countries to apply similar ideas.
